metadata.title: 1966 Case 30
metadata.original_presentation: Dr. Castleman: Will you continue with a description of the findings at operation, Dr. Yurchak? Dr. Yurchak: Dr. Bean and Dr. Katz may be surprised to learn that the operation was neither ligation of the inferior vena cava or the femoral veins nor an abdominal exploration, but open-heart surgery.

required.content: What was the initial suspected condition of the patient?
required.response: The patient was thought to have a pulmonary embolus but responded to conservative measures.

teaching_points.content: Pulmonary embolism can present with sudden onset of symptoms and may stabilize with anticoagulation and supportive care.

required.content: What was the patient's condition prior to surgery?
required.response: The patient's condition stabilized after a day and a half of conservative treatment.

teaching_points.content: Stabilization of a patient with suspected pulmonary embolism is crucial before proceeding with elective surgeries.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: stabilization of condition without surgical intervention specific to embolism
additional_information_needed: imaging studies such as CT pulmonary angiography

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cardiac Tamponade
refuting_evidence: no mention of classic triad symptoms

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Myocardial Infarction
supporting_evidence: open-heart surgery could suggest cardiac issue
refuting_evidence: no mention of chest pain or ECG changes

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Dissection
key_features: sudden severe chest or back pain
refuting_evidence: no mention of severe pain or pulse deficit
additional_information_needed: CT or MRI of the chest

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: stabilization of condition without surgical intervention
decision to perform open-heart surgery instead of addressing embolism directly
additional_information_needed: imaging results such as CT pulmonary angiography

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Cardiac Tamponade
supporting_evidence: stabilization with conservative treatment could suggest fluid management
refuting_evidence: lack of specific mention of classic triad symptoms

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Dissection
key_features: sudden severe chest or back pain
supporting_evidence: open-heart surgery could be related to aortic repair
refuting_evidence: stabilization with conservative treatment unlikely in acute dissection
additional_information_needed: CT or MRI of the chest

required.content: What were the findings during the operation?
required.response: Diffuse dilatation of the ascending aorta, normal aortic-valve leaflets, incompetent valve due to annulus dilatation, and tattered aortic intima.

teaching_points.content: Aortic aneurysms can lead to valve incompetence due to annular dilatation.

required.response: Large aneurysmal channel, linear tear, triangular pocket with flaps of intima, and destruction of the media.

teaching_points.content: Autopsy can reveal underlying pathologies such as old dissections and medial necrosis.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Dissection
supporting_evidence: triangular pocket with flaps of intima
additional_information_needed: patient's history of hypertension or connective tissue disorders
imaging studies such as CT or MRI

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Aneurysm
supporting_evidence: diffuse dilatation of the ascending aorta
refuting_evidence: tattered aortic intima suggests dissection rather than a simple aneurysm
additional_information_needed: imaging studies to confirm aneurysm size and extent

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Valve Insufficiency
supporting_evidence: incompetent valve due to annulus dilatation
refuting_evidence: primary issue appears to be dissection rather than isolated valve disease
additional_information_needed: patient's history of rheumatic fever or endocarditis

required.response: A large tuck was taken in the anterior wall of the aneurysm, aortic lumen was restored, and aortic-valve replacement was carried out.

teaching_points.content: Surgical intervention in aortic aneurysms may involve resection and valve replacement to restore function.

required.content: What was the underlying condition suspected in this case?
required.response: Annuloaortic ectasia of the ascending aorta due to medial disease.

teaching_points.content: Annuloaortic ectasia can lead to aortic dissection and aneurysm formation without external rupture.

final_diagnosis.name: Annuloaortic ectasia
key_features: Diffuse dilatation of the ascending aorta
supporting_evidence: Autopsy findings of aneurysmal channel and intimal tears
Surgical findings of dilated aortic annulus
refuting_evidence: No other signs of Marfan syndrome
